public_rationale: Google's May 30, 2024 explanation describes AI Overviews as integrating a language model with web search systems [e1]. This does not establish which material entered model training [e1]. On April 18, 2024, Meta described Llama 3's data filters, deduplication, and quality classifiers [e2]. Meta also disclosed synthetic training-data use that day [e3]. These disclosures establish neither declining nor stable selection standards across developers by the first half of 2024 [e1][e2][e3].
limitations: The packet lacks a comparable before-and-after audit or documented relaxation of training-data selection standards.
Meta's filtering descriptions are company disclosures, not independent quality audits.
The evidence does not establish an industry-wide trend or identify the training-data provenance of the cited search errors.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI developers have become less discerning about training data, ingesting unverified social posts, satire, and AI-generated content.

statement.excerpt: Already, we’ve seen AI developers become less discerning with the training data they use

our_interpretation: The plain reading is a deterioration in training-data selection standards, not simply the presence of imperfect material.
I use the first half of 2024 as the latest complete pre-publication observation window. The claimed change requires comparison with earlier practices.
Information retrieved while answering a search query is not necessarily training data.
Deliberately generated and screened synthetic training data does not by itself demonstrate reduced discernment.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable dataset audits or documented policy changes show developers relaxing training-data selection standards by the first half of 2024.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence across the relevant developers shows that selection standards remained stable or became stricter, contradicting the alleged deterioration.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable dataset audits or documented developer practices comparing earlier selection standards with those used in January–June 2024. They must distinguish training data from retrieved content and establish whether standards declined, remained stable, or improved across the relevant developers.
